newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan signs aviation pact with Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan signs aviation pact with Cambodia.

text.p: Taiwan has quietly signed a flight exchange pact with Cambodia, which maintains formal ties with the island's rival China, aviation officials said on Monday.

"We have officially signed the agreement with Kampuchea (Cambodia), which will allow both countries to operate commercial flights in the near future," a Civil Aeronautics Administration spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone.
She declined to say when the agreement was signed, but said the administration's director Tsay Ching-yen would make a formal announcement soon.
The local United Evening News, quoting an unidentified aviation official, said the accord was secretly signed by Tsay and his Cambodian counterpart in mid-December.
The agreement was official despite the absence of diplomatic relations between Taiwan and Cambodia, which recognises only the communist Chinese government in Beijing, the report said.

It said Taiwan agreed to sign the pact in secret to avoid pressure from China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province ineligible for international diplomatic ties since a civil war split them in 1949.
Under the agreement, each side will operate three flights weekly, with Taiwan's EVA Airways authorised to fly the Cambodia route beginning in March.
A spokeswoman for EVA, a unit of Evergreen Marine group TW, said the carrier had not received official notice.
"If we are given a green light, we plan to start the new route in March," she told Reuters by phone, adding that EVA would use either 767 or MD-90 wide-body jets for the service.
